maria: Quick heads up — I ran a hybrid INT4/FP8 KV run on llama-70b (commit 3b9a2f) using the new quant calibration. Memory dropped ~3.1x vs full FP16 KV but I'm seeing decode quality drift after ~700 tokens and intermittent p95 latency spikes when batch_size >= 8.

anil: Can you paste the perf snippet + how you calibrated? :eyes:

maria: Calibration steps: ran calibration on a 10k token prompt set, per-layer scale refit + per-head clamp. Command:
```
./tools/kv_calibrate --model=llama-70b --kv-format=hybrid-int4-fp8 --calib-corpus=~/data/kv_calib_10k.json --out=calib_v2.bin
```
Perf microbench (cold start -> warm):
```
batch=1  decode p50=18ms p95=22ms  alloc_kv=18GB
batch=8  decode p50=85ms p95=143ms alloc_kv=6GB
batch=8  (hybrid) decode p50=92ms p95=198ms alloc_kv=5.8GB
memory reduction ~3.1x
```

jade: Interesting that p95 jumped on hybrid for batch=8. Any kernel-switch logs? Could be GEMM path fallback.

maria: Yup, runtime logs show kernel selection thrash around token 720: switching between int4-isa and fp8-gemm for KV matmul. Snippet:
```
[perf] choose_kernel kv_matmul n=4096 k=128 -> int4_gemm
[perf] choose_kernel kv_matmul n=4096 k=256 -> fp8_gemm
[perf] choose_kernel kv_matmul n=4096 k=128 -> int4_gemm
```
That correlates with p95 spikes.

sam: That thrash suggests our heuristic is using sequence-length-dependent kernel picks; if KV quantization changes effective bitwidth per layer, the heuristic threshold should adapt. We saw similar in the 4-bit MLP work.

leo: Is the decode quality drift deterministic? Can you repro with fixed prompts and preserve RNG seed?

maria: Repro is consistent with same seed. Error mode is more token repetition and occasional broken tokens (subword fragmentation). Not catastrophic but visible on hallucination evals.

anil: Could be quantized KV accumulation overflow or clamp causing subtle attention weight shifts. Do we have per-layer max stats from calibration run?

maria: Yes, attached a trimmed table in the logs: layer 18 head 3 had scale=0.012, clamp hit rate=0.003. Most layers fine, a couple with higher clamp (~0.08) after 600 tokens.

jade: Two-pronged ask: (1) can we stabilize kernel selection (add hysteresis so we don't flip-flop within a single request) and (2) rerun calibration but with per-seq-length bucketed scales (short/medium/long) to see if dynamic calibration helps.

maria: Agreed. Proposing quick fixes: set kernel hysteresis window of 5 tokens and keep per-request kernel sticky; tune batching heuristic to prefer fp8_gemm for batch >=4 until steady-state.

sam: For measuring, add a microtrace tag to the runtime that logs kernel decisions + current seq_len + batch_idx. Also record timings per kernel.

perf-bot: Scheduled perf job: hybrid-kv-hysteresis-test queued on queue 'perf-rt-small' (job id 2026). Results expected in ~2h.

leo: If hysteresis fixes latency but not decode drift, then we need to update calibration. Try a per-head min-scale floor and quant-aware clamp smoothing.

maria: I'll run hysteresis job first. If it reduces p95 spikes by >25% keep as temporary mitigation. If decode quality persists, will run bucketed-calib. Will post results in this thread.

anil: Also file a small perf regression ticket so we track the regression vs baseline (attach logs + eval diffs). If anyone wants to pair on calibration tuning ping me.

maria: Thanks. cc @eng-runtime :thinking: I'll post the perf-job link when it's done.

(edited) maria: perf job finished: p95 reduced from 198ms->145ms on batch=8 with hysteresis, memory same. Still seeing small decode regressions; starting bucketed-calib now.

jade: Nice work. :thumbsup:

maria: Uploading bucketed calib artifacts to s3://redwood-dev/perf/hybrid_kv/bucketed_v1/

sam: Once you have eval diffs, let's run the quality/regression dashboard (small prompt set + longer reasoning set). Want numbers not anecdotes.

maria: Will do. Last note: if we go to int4-heavy KV, storage savings are huge, but we'll need to harden kernel selection heuristics and calibration flow before enabling per-request hybrid by default.

leo: Agreed. Keep updates here.
